rows.question: Please generate a summary of the closing balances at the end of each month for each customer transactions, show the monthly changes and monthly cumulative bank account balances. Ensure that even if a customer has no account activity in a given month, the balance for that month is still included in the output.
rows.error: OperationalError: misuse of window function SUM()
rows.pred_sql:
WITH
-- get overall min and max txn_date as proper dates
bounds AS (
  SELECT
    date(min(txn_date)) AS min_date,
    date(max(txn_date)) AS max_date
  FROM customer_transactions
),
-- recursive months series from min_date to max_date (inclusive)
months AS (
  SELECT date(min_date) AS month_date FROM bounds
  UNION ALL
  SELECT date(month_date, '+1 month') FROM months, bounds WHERE month_date < bounds.max_date
),
months_ym AS (
  SELECT substr(month_date,1,7) AS month FROM months
),
customers AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions
),
-- cross join customers x months to ensure every month appears for every customer
calendar AS (
  SELECT c.customer_id, m.month
  FROM customers c CROSS JOIN months_ym m
),
-- monthly aggregated net change per customer
monthly_txn AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    substr(date(txn_date),1,7) AS month,
    SUM(txn_amount) AS month_net_change
  FROM customer_transactions
  GROUP BY customer_id, substr(date(txn_date),1,7)
),
-- closing balance per customer per month: cumulative sum of month_net_change ordered by month
closing_per_cust AS (
  SELECT
    cal.customer_id,
    cal.month,
    COALESCE(mt.month_net_change,0) AS month_net_change
  FROM calendar cal
  LEFT JOIN monthly_txn mt
    ON cal.customer_id = mt.customer_id AND cal.month = mt.month
)
SELECT
  cpc.customer_id,
  cpc.month,
  -- closing balance at end of month for the customer: running sum over months for that customer
  SUM(cpc.month_net_change) OVER (
    PARTITION BY cpc.customer_id
    ORDER BY cpc.month
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  ) AS closing_balance,
  -- monthly change: difference between this month's closing balance and previous month's closing balance
  SUM(cpc.month_net_change) OVER (
    PARTITION BY cpc.customer_id
    ORDER BY cpc.month
    ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
  )
  -
  LAG(
    SUM(cpc.month_net_change) OVER (
      PARTITION BY cpc.customer_id
      ORDER BY cpc.month
      ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    )
  ) OVER (PARTITION BY cpc.customer_id ORDER BY cpc.month) AS monthly_change,
  -- cumulative bank account balance across all customers up through and including this month
  SUM(
    SUM(cpc.month_net_change) OVER (
      PARTITION BY cpc.customer_id
      ORDER BY cpc.month
      ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    )
  ) OVER (ORDER BY cpc.month ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS monthly_cumulative_bank_balance
FROM closing_per_cust cpc
ORDER BY cpc.customer_id, cpc.month

rows.question: For each customer and each month of 2020, first calculate the month-end balance by adding all deposit amounts and subtracting all withdrawal amounts that occurred during that specific month. Then determine which month in 2020 has the highest count of customers with a positive month-end balance and which month has the lowest count. For each of these two months, compute the average month-end balance across all customers and provide the difference between these two averages
rows.pred_sql:
WITH txns_2020 AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(txn_date) AS txn_date,
    strftime('%Y', date(txn_date)) AS year,
    strftime('%m', date(txn_date)) AS month,
    CASE LOWER(txn_type)
      WHEN 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
      WHEN 'withdrawal' THEN -txn_amount
      WHEN 'withdraw' THEN -txn_amount
      ELSE CASE WHEN txn_type LIKE '%dep%' THEN txn_amount
                WHEN txn_type LIKE '%with%' THEN -txn_amount
                ELSE 0 END
    END AS signed_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE date(txn_date) BETWEEN '2020-01-01' AND '2020-12-31'
),
cust_month_balances AS (
  -- per customer per month in 2020, the month-end balance (sum of signed amounts in that month)
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    month AS month_id,
    SUM(signed_amount) AS month_end_balance
  FROM txns_2020
  WHERE year = '2020'
  GROUP BY customer_id, month
),
-- ensure customers with no transactions in a month are treated as zero balance:
all_customers AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions
),
months AS (
  SELECT '01' AS month_id UNION ALL SELECT '02' UNION ALL SELECT '03' UNION ALL SELECT '04'
  UNION ALL SELECT '05' UNION ALL SELECT '06' UNION ALL SELECT '07' UNION ALL SELECT '08'
  UNION ALL SELECT '09' UNION ALL SELECT '10' UNION ALL SELECT '11' UNION ALL SELECT '12'
),
cust_month_grid AS (
  SELECT a.customer_id, m.month_id
  FROM all_customers a CROSS JOIN months m
),
cust_month_full AS (
  SELECT
    g.customer_id,
    g.month_id,
    COALESCE(b.month_end_balance, 0) AS month_end_balance
  FROM cust_month_grid g
  LEFT JOIN cust_month_balances b
    ON b.customer_id = g.customer_id AND b.month_id = g.month_id
),
month_stats AS (
  SELECT
    month_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN month_end_balance > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS positive_count,
    AVG(month_end_balance) AS avg_balance
  FROM cust_month_full
  GROUP BY month_id
)
SELECT
  max_m.month_id AS max_month,
  max_m.positive_count AS max_month_positive_customer_count,
  max_m.avg_balance AS max_month_avg_month_end_balance,
  min_m.month_id AS min_month,
  min_m.positive_count AS min_month_positive_customer_count,
  min_m.avg_balance AS min_month_avg_month_end_balance,
  (max_m.avg_balance - min_m.avg_balance) AS average_difference
FROM
  (SELECT month_id, positive_count, avg_balance FROM month_stats ORDER BY positive_count DESC, month_id ASC LIMIT 1) AS max_m,
  (SELECT month_id, positive_count, avg_balance FROM month_stats ORDER BY positive_count ASC, month_id ASC LIMIT 1) AS min_m

rows.question: For each customer, group all deposits and withdrawals by the first day of each month to obtain a monthly net amount, then calculate each month’s closing balance by cumulatively summing these monthly nets. Next, determine the most recent month’s growth rate by comparing its closing balance to the prior month’s balance, treating deposits as positive and withdrawals as negative, and if the previous month’s balance is zero, the growth rate should be the current month’s balance multiplied by 100. Finally, compute the percentage of customers whose most recent month shows a growth rate of more than 5%.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH txns AS (
  -- normalize txn_date to first day of month and sign amounts
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(substr(txn_date, 1, 10), 'start of month') AS month_first_day,
    CASE
      WHEN lower(txn_type) IN ('deposit','buy','credit') THEN txn_amount
      WHEN lower(txn_type) IN ('withdrawal','withdraw','sell','debit') THEN -txn_amount
      ELSE
        -- if txn_type unknown, treat deposits as positive if text contains deposit-like words
        CASE
          WHEN lower(txn_type) LIKE '%deposit%' THEN txn_amount
          WHEN lower(txn_type) LIKE '%withdraw%' THEN -txn_amount
          ELSE txn_amount
        END
    END AS signed_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
),
monthly_net AS (
  -- sum per customer per month
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    month_first_day,
    SUM(signed_amount) AS monthly_net
  FROM txns
  GROUP BY customer_id, month_first_day
),
monthly_closing AS (
  -- cumulative sum of monthly_net ordered by month to get closing balance at month end (using window)
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    month_first_day,
    monthly_net,
    SUM(monthly_net) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_first_day ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS closing_balance
  FROM monthly_net
),
most_recent AS (
  -- find the most recent month and the prior month closing balances per customer
  SELECT
    m.customer_id,
    m.month_first_day AS most_month,
    m.closing_balance AS most_recent_closing_balance,
    p.closing_balance AS prior_closing_balance
  FROM (
    SELECT customer_id, month_first_day, closing_balance,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_first_day DESC) AS rn
    FROM monthly_closing
  ) m
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT customer_id, month_first_day, closing_balance,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY month_first_day DESC) AS rn
    FROM monthly_closing
  ) p
  ON m.customer_id = p.customer_id AND p.rn = 2
  WHERE m.rn = 1
)
SELECT
  100.0
  * SUM(CASE
          WHEN (
            CASE
              WHEN COALESCE(prior_closing_balance, 0) != 0
                THEN (most_recent_closing_balance - COALESCE(prior_closing_balance, 0)) / COALESCE(prior_closing_balance, 0)
              ELSE most_recent_closing_balance * 100.0
            END
          ) > 0.05 THEN 1.0
          ELSE 0.0
        END)
  / COUNT(*) AS percentage_of_customers_with_most_recent_month_growth_rate_gt_5
FROM most_recent

rows.question: For each month, calculate the total balance from all users for the previous month (measured as of the 1st of each month), replacing any negative balances with zero. Ensure that data from the first month is used only as a baseline for calculating previous total balance, and exclude it from the final output. Sort the results in ascending order by month.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH -- parse txn_date to month (YYYY-MM) and get per-customer latest balance as of each date
txns AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(txn_date) AS txn_date,
    substr(date(txn_date),1,7) AS month
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE txn_type = 'balance'
),
-- For each customer and month, get the balance on that date (assuming txn_amount is the balance record)
cust_month_balance AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    month,
    txn_date,
    txn_amount AS balance
  FROM customer_transactions
  JOIN txns USING(customer_id, txn_date)
  WHERE txn_type = 'balance'
),
-- Determine the first month present (baseline), which we will exclude from output but use to compute previous totals
months_list AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT month FROM cust_month_balance
),
first_month AS (
  SELECT MIN(month) AS month FROM months_list
),
-- For each month and customer get the balance measured on the 1st of that month if exists,
-- otherwise use the latest balance prior to that month (measured as of the 1st)
measurement_dates AS (
  SELECT
    m.month,
    date(m.month || '-01') AS measure_date
  FROM (SELECT DISTINCT month FROM months_list) m
),
-- For each customer and measurement month, pick the latest balance record with txn_date < measure_date
cust_prev_balance AS (
  SELECT
    md.month,
    cmb.customer_id,
    cmb.balance,
    cmb.txn_date,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY md.month, cmb.customer_id ORDER BY date(cmb.txn_date) DESC) rn
  FROM measurement_dates md
  JOIN cust_month_balance cmb
    ON date(cmb.txn_date) < date(md.measure_date)
),
-- Keep only the latest per customer per month (previous month balance as of 1st)
cust_prev_latest AS (
  SELECT month, customer_id,
         CASE WHEN balance < 0 THEN 0 ELSE balance END AS balance_nonneg
  FROM cust_prev_balance
  WHERE rn = 1
),
-- Sum balances across customers for each month (this yields "previous month total balance" measured as of the 1st)
monthly_prev_totals AS (
  SELECT
    month,
    COALESCE(SUM(balance_nonneg),0) AS previous_month_total_balance
  FROM cust_prev_latest
  GROUP BY month
)
-- Exclude the first month from output and sort ascending
SELECT
  mpt.month,
  mpt.previous_month_total_balance
FROM monthly_prev_totals mpt
LEFT JOIN first_month fm ON mpt.month = fm.month
WHERE fm.month IS NULL
ORDER BY mpt.month ASC

rows.question: For a bank database with customer transactions, calculate each customer's daily running balance (where deposits add to the balance and other transaction types subtract). For each customer and each day, compute the 30-day rolling average balance (only after having 30 days of data, and treating negative averages as zero). Then group these daily averages by month and find each customer's maximum 30-day average balance within each month. Sum these maximum values across all customers for each month. Consider the first month of each customer's transaction history as the baseline period and exclude it from the final results, presenting monthly totals of these summed maximum 30-day average balances.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH chunk_view_0 AS (
SELECT
  ct.customer_id,
  ct.txn_date,
  ct.txn_type,
  ct.txn_amount
FROM customer_transactions ct
),
chunk_view_1 AS (
SELECT
  "txn_customer_id",
  "txn_date",
  "txn_type",
  "amount"
FROM "veg_txn_df"
)
SELECT
  month,
  SUM(max_30day_avg_nonneg) AS sum_max_30day_avg_balances
FROM (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    month,
    MAX(CASE WHEN rolling_count = 30 THEN CASE WHEN rolling_avg < 0 THEN 0.0 ELSE rolling_avg END END) AS max_30day_avg_nonneg
  FROM (
    SELECT
      customer_id,
      strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date) AS month,
      txn_date AS day,
      AVG(daily_balance) OVER (
        PARTITION BY customer_id
        ORDER BY txn_date
        ROWS BETWEEN 29 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
      ) AS rolling_avg,
      COUNT(daily_balance) OVER (
        PARTITION BY customer_id
        ORDER BY txn_date
        ROWS BETWEEN 29 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
      ) AS rolling_count,
      FIRST_VALUE(strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date)) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY txn_date ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS first_month
    FROM (
      SELECT
        customer_id,
        txn_date,
        SUM(CASE WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount ELSE -txn_amount END) AS daily_balance
      FROM customer_transactions
      GROUP BY customer_id, txn_date
    ) daily_balances
  ) with_roll
  WHERE month <> first_month
  GROUP BY customer_id, month
)
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month ASC

rows.question: For each customer, calculate their daily balances for every day between their earliest and latest transaction dates, including days without transactions by carrying forward the previous day's balance. Treat any negative daily balances as zero. Then, for each month, determine the highest daily balance each customer had during that month. Finally, for each month, sum these maximum daily balances across all customers to obtain a monthly total.

WITH
-- normalize transaction dates to ISO YYYY-MM-DD
txns AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(substr(txn_date, -4) || '-' || 
         printf('%02d', CASE instr(txn_date, '/') WHEN 0 THEN cast(strftime('%m', txn_date) AS INTEGER) ELSE cast(substr(txn_date, instr(txn_date,'/')+1, instr(txn_date,'/', instr(txn_date,'/')+1) - instr(txn_date,'/') -1) AS INTEGER) END) || '-' ||
         printf('%02d', CASE instr(txn_date, '/') WHEN 0 THEN cast(strftime('%d', txn_date) AS INTEGER) ELSE cast(substr(txn_date, 1, instr(txn_date,'/')-1) AS INTEGER) END)
        ) AS txn_date_iso,
    txn_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
),
-- If txn_date is already ISO-like (YYYY-MM-DD), try to use it directly as date(). Fallback: try common formats.
txns2 AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    CASE
      WHEN length(txn_date) = 10 AND substr(txn_date,5,1) = '-' THEN date(txn_date)
      WHEN instr(txn_date,'/') > 0 THEN date(
         substr(txn_date, instr(txn_date,'/', instr(txn_date,'/')+1)+1, 2) || '-' ||
         substr(txn_date, instr(txn_date,'/')+1, instr(txn_date,'/', instr(txn_date,'/')+1) - instr(txn_date,'/') -1) || '-' ||
         substr(txn_date, 1, instr(txn_date,'/')-1)
      )
      ELSE date(txn_date)
    END AS txn_date,
    txn_amount
  FROM (
    SELECT customer_id, txn_date, txn_amount FROM customer_transactions
  )
),
-- Use txns2 (more robust)
tx AS (
  SELECT customer_id, date(txn_date) AS txn_date, txn_amount
  FROM txns2
),
-- get date range per customer
cust_ranges AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    min(txn_date) AS start_date,
    max(txn_date) AS end_date
  FROM tx
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
-- generate calendar of dates per customer using recursive CTE
cust_calendar AS (
  SELECT customer_id, start_date AS cal_date, end_date
  FROM cust_ranges
  UNION ALL
  SELECT customer_id, date(cal_date, '+1 day') AS cal_date, end_date
  FROM cust_calendar
  WHERE cal_date < end_date
),
-- sum transactions per customer per day (in case multiple txns)
daily_txn AS (
  SELECT customer_id, txn_date AS cal_date, sum(txn_amount) AS daily_txn_amount
  FROM tx
  GROUP BY customer_id, txn_date
),
-- left join calendar with daily transactions
daily_with_txn AS (
  SELECT c.customer_id, c.cal_date, coalesce(d.daily_txn_amount,0) AS daily_txn_amount
  FROM cust_calendar c
  LEFT JOIN daily_txn d
    ON c.customer_id = d.customer_id AND c.cal_date = d.cal_date
),
-- compute running cumulative balance per customer, carrying forward; negative -> zero
running_balance AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    cal_date,
    -- compute cumulative sum of daily_txn_amount ordered by date per customer
    (SELECT 
       CASE WHEN coalesce(sum(daily_txn_amount),0) < 0 THEN 0 ELSE sum(daily_txn_amount) END
     FROM daily_with_txn d2
     WHERE d2.customer_id = d1.customer_id AND d2.cal_date <= d1.cal_date
    ) AS daily_balance
  FROM daily_with_txn d1
),
-- extract month (YYYY-MM) and find each customer's max daily balance per month
cust_month_max AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    substr(cal_date,1,7) AS month,
    max(daily_balance) AS max_daily_balance
  FROM running_balance
  GROUP BY customer_id, substr(cal_date,1,7)
),
-- sum across customers per month
monthly_totals AS (
  SELECT
    month,
    sum(max_daily_balance) AS monthly_total_max_daily_balance
  FROM cust_month_max
  GROUP BY month
)
SELECT month, monthly_total_max_daily_balance
FROM monthly_totals
ORDER BY month

rows.question: Can you provide a breakdown of how many times each product was viewed, how many times they were added to the shopping cart, and how many times they were left in the cart without being purchased? Also, give me the count of actual purchases for each product. Ensure that products with a page id in (1, 2, 12, 13) are filtered out.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH chunk_view_1 AS (
SELECT
  scph.product_id,
  scph.page_id,
  scph.page_name,
  sce.visit_id,
  sce.cookie_id,
  sce.event_type,
  sce.sequence_number,
  sce.event_time
FROM shopping_cart_page_hierarchy scph
JOIN shopping_cart_events sce
  ON scph.page_id = sce.page_id
WHERE scph.page_id NOT IN (1, 2, 12, 13)
),
chunk_view_2 AS (
SELECT
  scei.event_type AS event_type,
  scei.event_name AS event_name
FROM
  shopping_cart_event_identifier scei
)
SELECT
  p.product_id AS product_id,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN e.event_name = 'Page View' THEN 1 END) AS view_count,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN e.event_name = 'Add to Cart' THEN 1 END) AS add_to_cart_count,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN e.event_name = 'Left in Cart' THEN 1 END) AS left_in_cart_count,
  COUNT(CASE WHEN e.event_name IN ('Purchase','Order Complete') THEN 1 END) AS purchase_count
FROM shopping_cart_events ev
JOIN shopping_cart_page_hierarchy p ON ev.page_id = p.page_id
JOIN shopping_cart_event_identifier e ON ev.event_type = e.event_type
WHERE p.page_id NOT IN (1,2,12,13)
  AND p.product_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY p.product_id
ORDER BY p.product_id

rows.question: Please analyze our interest data from September 2018 to August 2019. For each month, calculate the average composition for each interest by dividing the composition by the index value. Identify the interest with the highest average composition value each month and report its average composition as the max index composition for that month. Compute the three-month rolling average of these monthly max index compositions. Ensure the output includes the date, the interest name, the max index composition for that month, the rolling average, and the names and max index compositions of the top interests from one month ago and two months ago.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH valid_interest AS (
  SELECT
    month_year,
    _month,
    _year,
    interest_id,
    composition,
    index_value,
    (composition / index_value) AS comp_over_index
  FROM interest_metrics
  WHERE index_value IS NOT NULL
    AND index_value != 0
    AND month_year IS NOT NULL
    -- limit to months between 09-2018 and 08-2019 inclusive
    AND (
      (CAST(_year AS INTEGER) = 2018 AND CAST(_month AS INTEGER) >= 9)
      OR (CAST(_year AS INTEGER) = 2019 AND CAST(_month AS INTEGER) <= 8)
    )
),
interest_month_avg AS (
  -- average composition/index per interest per month
  SELECT
    month_year,
    printf('%04d-%02d', CAST(_year AS INTEGER), CAST(_month AS INTEGER)) AS month_ym,
    interest_id,
    AVG(comp_over_index) AS avg_comp_index
  FROM valid_interest
  GROUP BY month_year, month_ym, interest_id
),
month_top_interest AS (
  -- pick top interest per month (highest avg_comp_index)
  SELECT
    ima.month_ym AS date,
    ima.interest_id,
    ima.avg_comp_index AS max_index_composition,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ima.month_ym ORDER BY ima.avg_comp_index DESC, ima.interest_id) AS rn
  FROM interest_month_avg AS ima
),
month_top_filtered AS (
  SELECT mti.date, mti.interest_id, mti.max_index_composition
  FROM month_top_interest mti
  WHERE mti.rn = 1
),
with_names AS (
  -- join to interest_map to get names
  SELECT
    mtf.date,
    im.interest_name,
    mtf.max_index_composition
  FROM month_top_filtered mtf
  LEFT JOIN interest_map im
    ON im.id = mtf.interest_id
),
ordered AS (
  SELECT
    date,
    interest_name,
    max_index_composition,
    -- row number over chronological order to enable lag by month position
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY date) AS seqnum
  FROM with_names
),
lagged AS (
  SELECT
    o.date,
    o.interest_name,
    o.max_index_composition,
    -- previous month (1) by available months (not calendar continuity)
    LAG(o.interest_name, 1) OVER (ORDER BY o.date) AS prev1_interest_name,
    LAG(o.max_index_composition, 1) OVER (ORDER BY o.date) AS prev1_max_index_composition,
    LAG(o.interest_name, 2) OVER (ORDER BY o.date) AS prev2_interest_name,
    LAG(o.max_index_composition, 2) OVER (ORDER BY o.date) AS prev2_max_index_composition,
    -- rolling average over this and two prior rows (only if three exist, else NULL)
    CASE
      WHEN COUNT(o.max_index_composition) OVER (ORDER BY o.date ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) = 3
      THEN AVG(o.max_index_composition) OVER (ORDER BY o.date ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
      ELSE NULL
    END AS rolling_average
  FROM ordered o
)
SELECT
  date,
  interest_name,
  max_index_composition,
  rolling_average,
  prev1_interest_name,
  prev1_max_index_composition,
  prev2_interest_name,
  prev2_max_index_composition
FROM lagged
ORDER BY date

rows.question: Analyze the annual average purchase price per Bitcoin by region, computed as the total dollar amount spent divided by the total quantity purchased each year, excluding the first year's data for each region. Then, for each year, rank the regions based on these average purchase prices, and calculate the annual percentage change in cost for each region compared to the previous year.

WITH tx AS (
  -- parse year and join member region
  SELECT
    substr(txn_date, -4) AS year, -- txn_date like 01-01-2017 or similar; take last 4 chars
    b.member_id,
    m.region AS region,
    b.txn_type,
    b.quantity,
    -- assume txn_type 'BUY' counts as purchase; ignore other types
    -- amount spent isn't in bitcoin_transactions; infer amount = quantity * price on txn_date by joining prices
    b.txn_time,
    b.ticker,
    b.txn_date
  FROM bitcoin_transactions b
  LEFT JOIN bitcoin_members m ON b.member_id = m.member_id
  WHERE b.txn_type = 'BUY'
),
price_on_date AS (
  -- normalize bitcoin_prices.market_date to a 4-digit year similar to txn_date format
  -- market_date examples are like 29-08-2021; take last 4 chars for year
  SELECT
    market_date,
    substr(market_date, -4) AS year,
    ticker,
    price
  FROM bitcoin_prices
),
tx_with_price AS (
  -- join each buy txn to the price row for the same year and ticker to estimate dollars spent
  SELECT
    t.year,
    t.region,
    t.quantity,
    p.price,
    (t.quantity * p.price) AS dollars_spent
  FROM tx t
  LEFT JOIN price_on_date p
    ON p.year = t.year
    AND p.ticker = t.ticker
  WHERE p.price IS NOT NULL
),
annual_region AS (
  -- aggregate per region-year
  SELECT
    CAST(year AS INTEGER) AS year,
    region,
    SUM(dollars_spent) AS total_dollars,
    SUM(quantity) AS total_quantity,
    CASE WHEN SUM(quantity) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE SUM(dollars_spent) / SUM(quantity) END AS avg_price_per_bitcoin
  FROM tx_with_price
  GROUP BY CAST(year AS INTEGER), region
),
ranked AS (
  -- rank regions within each year by avg price desc (highest price = rank 1)
  SELECT
    ar.*,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY avg_price_per_bitcoin DESC) AS rank_within_year
  FROM annual_region ar
),
with_pct AS (
  -- join prior year to compute pct change; exclude first year per region by leaving pct NULL when no prior
  SELECT
    cur.year,
    cur.region,
    cur.avg_price_per_bitcoin,
    cur.rank_within_year,
    CASE
      WHEN prev.avg_price_per_bitcoin IS NULL THEN NULL
      WHEN prev.avg_price_per_bitcoin = 0 THEN NULL
      ELSE (cur.avg_price_per_bitcoin - prev.avg_price_per_bitcoin) / prev.avg_price_per_bitcoin * 100.0
    END AS pct_change_from_prev_year
  FROM ranked cur
  LEFT JOIN ranked prev
    ON prev.region = cur.region
    AND prev.year = cur.year - 1
)
SELECT
  year,
  region,
  avg_price_per_bitcoin,
  rank_within_year,
  pct_change_from_prev_year
FROM with_pct
WHERE avg_price_per_bitcoin IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY year ASC, rank_within_year ASC

rows.question: Using the "bitcoin_prices" table, please calculate the daily percentage change in trading volume for each ticker from August 1 to August 10, 2021, ensuring that any volume ending in "K" or "M" is accurately converted to thousands or millions, any "-" volume is treated as zero, only non-zero volumes are used to determine the previous day's volume, and the results are ordered by ticker and date.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH parsed AS (
  SELECT
    ticker,
    -- normalize market_date from formats like '29-08-2021' to '2021-08-29' for easy comparison
    -- assume market_date is in DD-MM-YYYY format
    substr(market_date, 7, 4) || '-' || substr(market_date, 4, 2) || '-' || substr(market_date, 1, 2) AS date,
    market_date AS date_raw,
    volume AS volume_raw,
    -- convert volume_raw: '-' -> 0, '123K'->123000, '4.5M'->4500000, numeric strings -> as number
    CASE
      WHEN trim(volume) = '-' THEN 0.0
      WHEN volume LIKE '%K' THEN
        -- remove trailing K and parse as number * 1000
        CAST(replace(volume, 'K', '') AS REAL) * 1000.0
      WHEN volume LIKE '%M' THEN
        CAST(replace(volume, 'M', '') AS REAL) * 1000000.0
      ELSE
        -- fallback: try cast to real (handles plain numeric strings)
        CAST(volume AS REAL)
    END AS volume_converted
  FROM bitcoin_prices
), filtered AS (
  -- keep only dates in range 2021-08-01 .. 2021-08-10 and ensure date parsing produced valid dates
  SELECT *
  FROM parsed
  WHERE date BETWEEN '2021-08-01' AND '2021-08-10'
), prev_nonzero AS (
  -- for each row find the most recent prior date for the same ticker with volume_converted > 0
  SELECT
    f.ticker,
    f.date,
    f.date_raw AS market_date,
    f.volume_raw,
    f.volume_converted,
    (
      SELECT p.volume_converted
      FROM filtered p
      WHERE p.ticker = f.ticker
        AND p.date < f.date
        AND p.volume_converted > 0
      ORDER BY p.date DESC
      LIMIT 1
    ) AS prev_nonzero_volume
  FROM filtered f
)
SELECT
  ticker,
  date AS date,
  volume_raw,
  volume_converted,
  prev_nonzero_volume,
  CASE
    WHEN prev_nonzero_volume IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN prev_nonzero_volume = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE ((volume_converted - prev_nonzero_volume) / prev_nonzero_volume) * 100.0
  END AS daily_pct_change
FROM prev_nonzero
ORDER BY ticker ASC, date ASC

rows.question: For veg whsle data, can you generate a summary of our items' loss rates? Include the average loss rate, and also break down the count of items that are below, above, and within one standard deviation from this average.
rows.error: OperationalError: misuse of aggregate function AVG()

WITH per_item AS (
  SELECT
    item_code,
    AVG("loss_rate_%") AS item_loss_rate
  FROM veg_loss_rate_df
  WHERE "loss_rate_%" IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY item_code
),
stats AS (
  SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS total_items,
    AVG(item_loss_rate) AS average_loss_rate,
    CASE
      WHEN COUNT(*) > 1 THEN
        -- sample standard deviation: sqrt( sum((x-mean)^2) / (n-1) )
        SQRT( SUM( (item_loss_rate - AVG(item_loss_rate))*(item_loss_rate - AVG(item_loss_rate)) ) / (COUNT(*) - 1) )
      ELSE 0.0
    END AS loss_rate_stddev
  FROM per_item
)
SELECT
  s.average_loss_rate,
  s.loss_rate_stddev,
  SUM(CASE WHEN p.item_loss_rate < s.average_loss_rate - s.loss_rate_stddev THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_below_one_std_below_mean,
  SUM(CASE WHEN p.item_loss_rate >= s.average_loss_rate - s.loss_rate_stddev
           AND p.item_loss_rate <= s.average_loss_rate + s.loss_rate_stddev THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_within_one_std,
  SUM(CASE WHEN p.item_loss_rate > s.average_loss_rate + s.loss_rate_stddev THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_above_one_std_above_mean,
  s.total_items
FROM per_item p
CROSS JOIN stats s

rows.question: Which university faculty members' salaries are closest to the average salary for their respective ranks? Please provide the ranks, first names, last names, and salaries.university
rows.pred_sql:
WITH chunk_view_0 AS (
SELECT
  OfferNo,
  StdNo,
  EnrGrade
FROM
  university_enrollment
),
chunk_view_1 AS (
SELECT
  FacNo,
  FacFirstName,
  FacLastName,
  FacRank,
  FacSalary
FROM university_faculty
)
SELECT
  f.FacRank AS rank,
  f.FacFirstName AS first_name,
  f.FacLastName AS last_name,
  f.FacSalary AS salary
FROM university_faculty f
JOIN (
  SELECT
    FacRank,
    MIN(ABS(FacSalary - avg_salary)) AS min_abs_diff
  FROM (
    SELECT
      uf.FacRank,
      uf.FacSalary,
      (SELECT AVG(FacSalary) FROM university_faculty WHERE FacRank = uf.FacRank) AS avg_salary
    FROM university_faculty uf
  )
  GROUP BY FacRank
) m
  ON f.FacRank = m.FacRank
WHERE ABS(f.FacSalary - (SELECT AVG(FacSalary) FROM university_faculty WHERE FacRank = f.FacRank)) = m.min_abs_diff
ORDER BY rank

rows.question: Using a Salary Dataset where the salary values need to be cleaned by removing non-numeric characters and converting them to a numeric type, write a detailed SQL query that identifies the top 5 companies by average salary in each of Mumbai, Pune, New Delhi, and Hyderabad, then compares each company’s average salary in those cities to the overall national average salary. The final result should display four columns: Location, Company Name, Average Salary in State, and Average Salary in Country, listing only the top 5 companies in each of the specified locations.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH cleaned AS (
  -- Clean SalaryDataset salaries by removing non-numeric characters.
  -- SQLite doesn't have regexp_replace, so we remove common non-numeric characters explicitly.
  -- This handles typical formats like "₹6,48,573/yr" or "1191950" or "₹ 1,191,950 / yr"
  SELECT
    CompanyName,
    Location,
    -- remove currency symbol, commas, spaces, and "/yr" or "per year" text fragments
    NULLIF(
      TRIM(
        REPLACE(
          REPLACE(
            REPLACE(
              REPLACE(
                REPLACE(
                  REPLACE(Salary, '₹', ''),     -- remove rupee symbol
                ',', ''),                       -- remove thousands separator
              '/yr', ''),                       -- remove /yr
            'per year', ''),                    -- remove textual per year
          ' ', ''),                             -- remove any spaces
        '/ year' , '' )                         -- remove possible variant
      ), '') AS salary_text
  FROM SalaryDataset
),
numeric AS (
  -- Convert cleaned text to numeric where possible. Use CAST; invalid conversions become 0 in some SQLite builds,
  -- so guard by checking that salary_text consists only of digits (using GLOB).
  SELECT
    CompanyName,
    Location,
    CASE
      WHEN salary_text IS NOT NULL AND salary_text GLOB '[0-9]*' AND salary_text <> '' THEN CAST(salary_text AS REAL)
      ELSE NULL
    END AS clean_salary
  FROM cleaned
),
location_company_avgs AS (
  -- Compute average salary per company per requested location
  SELECT
    Location,
    CompanyName,
    AVG(clean_salary) AS avg_state
  FROM numeric
  WHERE Location IN ('Mumbai', 'Pune', 'New Delhi', 'Hyderabad')
    AND clean_salary IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY Location, CompanyName
),
national_avg AS (
  -- Compute national average across all locations / companies
  SELECT AVG(clean_salary) AS avg_country
  FROM numeric
  WHERE clean_salary IS NOT NULL
),
ranked AS (
  -- Rank companies within each location by avg_state and keep row number for filtering top 5
  SELECT
    lca.Location,
    lca.CompanyName,
    lca.avg_state,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY lca.Location ORDER BY lca.avg_state DESC) AS rn
  FROM location_company_avgs lca
)
-- Final select: only top 5 per specified location, include national average for comparison
SELECT
  r.Location AS Location,
  r.CompanyName AS "Company Name",
  ROUND(r.avg_state, 2) AS "Average Salary in State",
  ROUND(n.avg_country, 2) AS "Average Salary in Country"
FROM ranked r
CROSS JOIN national_avg n
WHERE r.rn <= 5
ORDER BY r.Location, r.avg_state DESC
